x: Bimbisara of the Haryanka dynasty ruled Magadha in the Buddha's time and became his patron. Prasenjit was a contemporary too, but he ruled Kosala, not Magadha.
t: Discriminate the kings of Magadha and Kosala.

x: Both are true but R does not explain A: Dhanananda ruled Magadha when Alexander invaded in 326 BCE, and Greek writers called him Agrammes, but the name does not explain why they lived at the same time.
t: Check whether R is the cause of A.

x: Ashvaghosha wrote the Buddhacharita, Vasumitra presided over the Fourth Buddhist Council, Banabhatta wrote the Harshacharita and Ralph Fitch was the first English merchant at Akbar's court, giving a-iii, b-iv, c-i, d-ii.
t: Recall the work or role of each person.

x: Option C is incorrect: Ralph Fitch was in India from 1583 to 1586, not 1586 to 1589. He visited Agra and Fatehpur Sikri and was the first English merchant at Akbar's court.
t: Recall the dates of Ralph Fitch's visit.

x: Both are true: Shaikh Ahmad Sirhindi (1564–1624) lived under Akbar and Jahangir, and Shaikh Salim Chishti (1478–1572) was Akbar's spiritual guide at Sikri.

x: Four belonged to Kanishka's court: Ashvaghosha, Vasumitra, Nagarjuna and the physician Charaka. Banabhatta was the court poet of Harsha.

x: Namdev (1270–1350), Kabir (1398–1518), Guru Nanak (1469–1539) and Mirabai (1498–1546), giving C, A, D, B.
t: Arrange the saints by birth year.

x: The English East India Company received its charter from Queen Elizabeth I on 31 December 1600, during Akbar's reign (1556–1605).
t: Match the year with the ruler's reign.

x: Bhaddasala was the commander of Dhanananda, the last Nanda king, and was defeated by Chandragupta Maurya's forces. Vasumitra, Parsva and Mathara belong to Kanishka's court.
t: Recall the commander of the last Nanda king.

x: Both are true but R does not explain A: Patanjali wrote the Mahabhashya and lived under Pushyamitra Shunga, but writing the book does not explain why he lived in that reign.
t: Check whether R is the cause of A.

x: All four graced Kanishka's court: Nagarjuna expounded Madhyamika philosophy, Charaka wrote the Charaka Samhita, Ashvaghosha wrote the Buddhacharita and Vasumitra presided over the Fourth Buddhist Council, giving a-i, b-ii, c-iii, d-iv.
t: Recall each Kushana-court scholar's signature contribution.

 d. Vasumitra

x: Xuanzang (Hiuen Tsang) came to India in Harsha's reign, about 630–645 CE, and attended his assembly at Kanauj. Fa-Hien came under Chandragupta II.
t: Recall the ruler visited by each Chinese pilgrim.

x: Both are true but R does not explain A: Mirabai (1498–1546) overlapped with both Guru Nanak and Chaitanya, but her overlap with Chaitanya does not explain her overlap with Nanak.
t: Check whether R is the cause of A.

x: Both are true: Nasiruddin Chirag-i-Dehlavi (1274–1356) was the disciple and successor of Nizamuddin Auliya in the Chishti order at Delhi.
t: Check each statement separately.

x: Shaikh Ahmad Sirhindi lived 1564–1624, Salim Chishti 1478–1572, Nasiruddin Chirag-i-Dehlavi 1274–1356 and Mirabai 1498–1546, giving a-ii, b-iii, c-iv, d-i.
t: Recall the dates of each saint.

x: Tukaram (about 1608–1650), the Varkari saint of Maharashtra, lived under Jahangir and Shah Jahan. Akbar died in 1605, before Tukaram was born.
t: Compare the saint's dates with each reign.

x: Rock Edict XIII names Turamaya (Ptolemy II of Egypt), Antiyoka (Antiochus II of Syria), Antikini (Antigonus Gonatas of Macedonia) and Maka (Magas of Cyrene) as Ashoka's contemporaries, giving a-i, b-ii, c-iii, d-iv.
t: Match the Prakrit forms to the Greek names by sound.

x: Both are true: the Indus Civilisation (about 2600–1900 BCE) flourished at the same time as Mesopotamia and Old Kingdom Egypt, and traded with Mesopotamia.
t: Check each statement separately.

x: Both are true and R explains A: Akbar ruled 1556–1605 and Elizabeth I ruled 1558–1603, so the overlap of their reigns is what makes them contemporaries.
t: Check whether R is the cause of A.

x: Both are true: Mirabai (1498–1546) overlapped with Tulsidas (about 1532–1623), and Bimbisara of Magadha ruled in the time of Mahavira and the Buddha.

x: Both are true but R does not explain A: Makkhali Gosala led the Ajivikas and lived at the same time as Mahavira, but leading the sect does not explain that overlap.
t: Check whether R is the cause of A.

1. Magas
2. Alexander of Epirus

x: Chandragupta Maurya founded the Mauryan empire around 321 BCE. Do not confuse him with the Gupta king Chandragupta II, who ruled much later.
t: Discriminate Chandragupta Maurya from Chandragupta II.

x: Both are true: Salim Chishti lived at Sikri, where Akbar built Fatehpur Sikri, and Portuguese visitors such as Domingo Paes reached Vijayanagara under Krishnadeva Raya.
t: Check each statement separately.

x: All three are correct: Guru Arjan Dev was executed under Jahangir in 1606, Guru Tegh Bahadur under Aurangzeb in 1675, and Salim Chishti lived at Sikri in Akbar's time.
t: Check the ruler named in each statement.
s:
Consider the following statements:
I. Guru Arjan Dev's execution is associated with Jahangir.
II. Guru Tegh Bahadur's execution is associated with Aurangzeb.
III. Salim Chishti is associated with Sikri during Akbar's reign.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
